text: A 150-case dataset only helps if something can actually grade all 150 cases, every time, without a human reading every response. That's what automated eval metrics are for.

Real eval tools let you configure providers — the models or endpoints being tested — directly from a web UI. This is promptfoo, a widely-used open-source eval framework, showing its Choose Providers step before any grading rule gets written.

Exact match is fast but only works when there's one acceptable phrasing. Semantic similarity compares meaning using embeddings. LLM-as-judge has a second model grade output against a written rubric — what makes open-ended text practical to grade at scale. Accuracy, relevance, and faithfulness are the three that matter most for AI quality specifically.
Once an eval runs, a results view shows every test case's output side by side across providers, with a pass rate calculated automatically right at the top of each column.

Beyond the per-case table, these tools chart the aggregate numbers too — pass rate per provider, a score distribution, and two variants compared head-to-head. That's what makes a large run readable in seconds instead of a full manual review.
Next lesson: human evaluation processes — what automated metrics still can't catch, and how to build a review process that actually scales.
